wedding-checklist.title: Wedding Checklist: The Complete Planning Roadmap
wedding-checklist.description: Use a complete wedding checklist organized by decisions, dependencies, and deadlines - from first priorities through the final handoff.
wedding-checklist.h1: The wedding checklist that tells you what comes next
wedding-checklist.intro: A useful wedding checklist is not a pile of tasks. It is a decision sequence: lock the facts that control everything else, book the scarce vendors, connect payments to contracts, and keep the final week separate from long-range planning.
wedding-checklist.direct_answer: Start with the wedding date, guest-count range, location, budget ceiling, and who has decision authority. Then work in dependency order: venue and ceremony anchors, priority vendors, guest logistics, design and attire, final counts, payments, and the wedding-week handoff.

sections.heading: 1. Establish the five controlling facts
paragraphs: Confirm the wedding date or date window, the planning start date, the guest-count range, the location or venue search area, and the total amount you are prepared to spend. These inputs control vendor availability, lead times, capacity, and the pace of every later decision.
bullets: Guest-count range, not a false exact number

sections.heading: 2. Book the critical path before the decorative layer
paragraphs: Venue, ceremony access, planner or coordinator, catering, photography, and any high-priority entertainment usually create dependencies for the rest of the plan. Do not spend weeks on colors while the date, capacity, or core vendors remain unresolved.
bullets: Book the vendors with the least availability
Record deposits, due dates, and cancellation terms
Create one owner for every open decision

sections.heading: 3. Move from planning to handoff
paragraphs: The final month is not the time to keep redesigning the wedding. It is the time to reconcile guest counts, meals, accessibility needs, balances, arrivals, setup, transportation, emergency contacts, and the final timeline.
bullets: Freeze the guest list and seating inputs
Confirm final vendor counts and balances
Create one final version for vendors and family

rows: The controlling facts are written down
Guest, design, attire, and logistics workstreams active
Dependencies and due dates are assigned
Counts, payments, seating, and timeline reconciled
Every unresolved item has an owner
Vendors and key people acknowledge the final version

faqs.question: What should be first on a wedding checklist?
faqs.answer: The first items are the date or date window, guest-count range, location, budget ceiling, and decision owners. Those facts control almost every later task.

faqs.question: How far in advance should wedding planning start?
faqs.answer: Start when you are ready to make the controlling decisions. A longer runway creates more options, but a shorter runway can work when you prioritize the critical path and accept fewer vendor or date choices.

faqs.question: Should I use a 12-month checklist if my engagement is shorter?
faqs.answer: No. Use a checklist tied to the time you actually have. Compressed plans should prioritize legal, venue, vendor, guest, payment, and handoff dependencies rather than pretending every traditional lead time is still available.

wedding-planning-checklist.title: Wedding Planning Checklist: Step-by-Step Process
wedding-planning-checklist.description: Follow a step-by-step wedding planning checklist built around owners, dependencies, contracts, guest logistics, and final handoffs.
wedding-planning-checklist.eyebrow: A process, not a random to-do list
wedding-planning-checklist.h1: Wedding planning checklist: decisions in the right order
wedding-planning-checklist.intro: Wedding planning gets easier when every task has an owner, a deadline, and a reason it must happen before something else. This checklist groups the work into operating lanes so decisions stop getting lost across messages, notes, and vendor portals.
wedding-planning-checklist.direct_answer: Run the plan through six lanes: scope and authority, venue and vendor contracts, guest management, design and attire, money and payments, and wedding-week operations. Review all six lanes together once a week so a change in one lane is reflected everywhere else.

sections.heading: Build one operating plan
paragraphs: Use one master list with the task, owner, due date, status, dependency, cost, and link to the controlling document. Separate ideas from commitments: a saved inspiration image is not a vendor booking, and a verbal quote is not a contracted price.

sections.heading: Review by workstream, not by mood
paragraphs: A weekly review should scan each workstream for missing decisions, late deposits, unanswered vendor questions, guest changes, and handoff risks. This is more reliable than working only on whatever feels urgent that day.

sections.heading: Close decisions cleanly
paragraphs: Every decision should end with a documented selection, the reason, the cost or constraint, who was notified, and what downstream task changed. Clean closure prevents the same debate from reopening and stops multiple versions from circulating.

rows: What is unbooked, unsigned, or unanswered?
Which count, meal, travel, or accessibility inputs changed?
Which choices affect orders, rentals, or setup?
What is due next and what changed?
What must be handed off and to whom?

faqs.question: How do I organize a wedding planning checklist?
faqs.answer: Organize by workstream and dependency, then add an owner, due date, status, and controlling link to every task.

faqs.question: How often should we review the wedding plan?
faqs.answer: A weekly review is usually frequent enough during the main planning period. Increase the cadence in the final month or whenever multiple vendor deadlines converge.

faqs.question: Who should own wedding planning tasks?
faqs.answer: Assign one accountable owner even when several people help. Shared ownership without one final owner is a common reason tasks remain unresolved.

wedding-budget-spreadsheet.title: Wedding Budget Spreadsheet: What to Track + Paid Product Preview
wedding-budget-spreadsheet.description: Learn what a wedding budget spreadsheet should track and see actual watermarked previews of the paid Categories, Payments, Hidden Costs, summary, and cash-flow views.
wedding-budget-spreadsheet.eyebrow: Wedding budget method + real paid-product preview
wedding-budget-spreadsheet.intro: A wedding budget should show more than category targets. It should separate estimates from contracted amounts, track deposits and due dates, and show what cash is still required by month.
wedding-budget-spreadsheet.direct_answer: A useful wedding budget spreadsheet must separate estimates, contracts, payments, remaining balances, due dates, hidden costs, and cash timing. The paid product preview below shows those actual working views without exposing the editable file.

sections.heading: Build the budget around commitments
paragraphs: Start with a total ceiling and category targets, but switch to contracted amounts as agreements are signed. Never overwrite the estimate; the variance between estimate and contract is useful planning evidence.

sections.heading: Track cash timing, not just totals
paragraphs: A wedding can be under budget overall and still create a cash crunch when several deposits or final payments land in the same month. Group balances by due month and keep a separate line for taxes, service fees, gratuities, delivery, alterations, and returns.

sections.heading: Reconcile after every contract change
paragraphs: When scope, guest count, hours, quantities, or delivery terms change, update the contract amount, payment schedule, and related categories together. A budget that is not connected to current agreements is only a memory aid.

faqs.question: What should a wedding budget spreadsheet include?
faqs.answer: Include estimates, contracted amounts, taxes and fees, deposits, paid amounts, remaining balances, due dates, payer, category, vendor, and notes.

faqs.question: Can I use the paid workbook in Google Sheets?
faqs.answer: The purchase includes an XLSX workbook. Compatibility can vary by spreadsheet application, so verify formatting and data validation after importing into Google Sheets.

faqs.question: Does the spreadsheet include current vendor prices?
faqs.answer: No. Pricing varies by location, date, scope, and vendor. Enter verified quotes, contracts, and invoices.

wedding-timeline-template.description: Build a coordinated wedding-day schedule and see actual watermarked previews of the paid master timeline, vendor-arrival, role-handoff, and printable timeline pages.
wedding-timeline-template.eyebrow: Wedding-day scheduling method + real product preview
wedding-timeline-template.intro: A useful wedding timeline is a coordination document, not just a list of ceremony and reception moments. It connects locations, owners, vendor arrivals, setup, travel, photography, meals, and handoffs.
wedding-timeline-template.direct_answer: A usable wedding timeline needs a master schedule plus vendor arrivals, role-specific handoffs, locations, dependencies, buffers, and confirmations. The preview below shows those real paid-file views without giving away the editable template.

sections.heading: Start with immovable anchors
paragraphs: Confirm ceremony access, guest arrival, ceremony start, meal service, venue end time, transportation windows, and any religious or venue requirements. These anchors control the rest of the schedule.

sections.heading: Create role-specific views
paragraphs: The couple, wedding party, family, photographer, venue, caterer, and entertainment team do not need every line. Build one master schedule, then issue filtered handoffs that show what each person must know and do.

sections.heading: Protect transitions with buffers
paragraphs: Travel, outfit changes, room flips, receiving lines, elevator access, parking, and family-photo gathering take longer than the headline event. Add explicit buffers instead of hoping the schedule absorbs them.

faqs.question: What should be included in a wedding timeline?
faqs.answer: Include fixed anchors, preparation, vendor arrivals, setup, photography, travel, guest movement, ceremony, reception events, breakdown, owners, locations, and buffers.

faqs.question: How much buffer should a wedding timeline have?
faqs.answer: The right buffer depends on travel, venue access, group size, elevators, parking, photography, and setup. Confirm with the people responsible rather than applying one universal number.

faqs.answer: Yes. Import it into Google Sheets, Excel, Numbers, or another compatible spreadsheet tool.

wedding-seating-chart.title: Wedding Seating Chart Planner + Paid Product Preview
wedding-seating-chart.description: Learn how to build a venue-ready seating plan and see actual previews of the paid guest master, table reconciliation, vendor handoff, and printable seating worksheets.
wedding-seating-chart.eyebrow: Guest placement that survives final-week changes
wedding-seating-chart.intro: A seating chart is complete only when every confirmed guest is assigned or visibly unresolved, table capacities are respected, and the final data can be handed to the venue, caterer, and stationery team.
wedding-seating-chart.direct_answer: A seating chart should reconcile every confirmed guest against table capacity while carrying meals, allergies, accessibility needs, children, and vendor handoff details. The paid-product preview shows how those views are organized.

sections.heading: Use the confirmed guest list as the source of truth
paragraphs: Do not build from invitation drafts, text messages, or multiple spreadsheets. Each guest record should have one stable name, household or group, RSVP status, meal, allergy, accessibility, child/high-chair, and notes fields.

sections.heading: Build from venue capacity rules
paragraphs: Use the venue-approved floor plan and capacity guidance. Table labels, seat counts, dance-floor clearance, service paths, and accessibility routes must come from the venue or responsible professional, not from an online diagram.

sections.heading: Reconcile before printing
paragraphs: Compare confirmed RSVPs with assigned guests, then review meals, allergies, children, and accessibility data by table. Issue one frozen version and control every later change.
bullets: Every special need is attached to the correct guest

faqs.question: How do I make a wedding seating chart?
faqs.answer: Use one confirmed guest list, venue-approved table capacities, household and social grouping, special-needs fields, and a final reconciliation between confirmed and assigned guests.

faqs.question: How many people should sit at a wedding table?
faqs.answer: Capacity depends on table size, chairs, place settings, service style, room layout, and venue rules. Confirm the approved and comfortable capacity with the venue or rental provider.

faqs.question: When should the seating chart be final?
faqs.answer: Finalize after the venue and caterer require final counts, while leaving a controlled process for late cancellations or approved substitutions.

wedding-guest-list-template.title: Wedding Guest List Template: Required Fields + Paid Product Preview
wedding-guest-list-template.description: Learn which fields a wedding guest list needs for RSVPs, meals, accessibility, children, seating, and vendor handoff, then see the actual paid guest-master and reconciliation views.
wedding-guest-list-template.eyebrow: The source of truth behind seating and catering
wedding-guest-list-template.intro: A guest list should support invitations, RSVPs, catering, accessibility, seating, and final vendor handoff. This guide explains the required fields and shows a flattened preview of the paid guest-master and seating workflow without exposing the editable files.
wedding-guest-list-template.direct_answer: Use one guest record per person, preserve household/group context, and keep RSVP, meal, allergy, accessibility, child, seating, and confirmation data together. The paid product preview shows how those fields connect to table and vendor handoff views.

sections.heading: One person, one record
paragraphs: Household-level invitation tracking is useful, but catering and seating work at the person level. Separate adults, children, and plus-ones so each confirmed guest can be counted and assigned.

sections.heading: Keep unknowns visible
paragraphs: Do not guess a plus-one name, meal, or accessibility need. Mark the field unresolved and assign an owner to follow up. Hidden blanks are easy to miss; explicit unknowns can be managed.

sections.heading: Freeze the vendor handoff
paragraphs: Before sending to the venue or caterer, reconcile confirmed guests, meals, allergies, children, and assigned seats. Export only the fields each vendor needs and retain a dated master copy.

faqs.question: Should couples or households be one row in a guest list?
faqs.answer: Use one row per person for final operations. Keep a household field so invitations and communications can still be grouped.

faqs.question: What columns should a wedding guest list have?
faqs.answer: Include names, household, contact status, invitation status, RSVP, meal, allergy, accessibility, child/high-chair, table, notes, and follow-up owner as applicable.
